description: Write about pictures, tell stories, explain steps, and share your opinion.

A.studentGoal: I can write words and simple sentences about a picture.

info.headline: Write words and simple sentences about pictures and familiar topics
info.summary: Starting writers label pictures, copy and finish sentence frames, and write one or two simple sentences. They use word banks, pictures, and first-next-last to tell a story, give steps, or share an opinion. Every writing task can be done on paper, like the ACCESS writing booklet.
canDo: I can write a sentence that tells what I see in a picture.
I can use first, next, and last to tell a story.
I can write my opinion with because.
I can start a sentence with a capital letter and end it with a period.

categories.title: Write About Pictures
categories.desc: Describe a scene and tell picture stories with first, next, last.

categories.title: Steps, Facts, and Opinions
categories.desc: Write steps, facts about helpers, and an opinion with because.

categories.title: Build Strong Sentences
categories.desc: Fix verb forms, order a paragraph, and pick a complete sentence.

categories.title: Paper Practice
categories.desc: Printable pages with drawing boxes and writing lines.

activities.title: Write About the Park
activities.skill: Describe a picture with simple sentences
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the park. Write 1 or 2 sentences. Tell what you see and what the children are doing. You can write on paper too.
activities.prompt: Look at the picture of the park. What do you see? What are the children doing?

picture.alt: A sunny park with a tree, a girl on a swing, a boy kicking a red ball, a brown dog, and a bench.

activities.responsePlaceholder: I see a ___. The girl is ___.

models.A: I see a park. A girl is on the swing.
models.B: I see a sunny park with a big tree. A girl is on the swing. A boy is kicking a red ball, and a brown dog runs because it wants to play.
models.C: The park is a busy place on a sunny day. First, I see a girl swinging high next to a big green tree. A boy is kicking a red ball, and a brown dog is running after it. There is also an empty bench where people can rest. Everyone in the park looks happy to be outside.

vocabulary: an outdoor place with grass, trees, and things to play on
parque: un lugar al aire libre con pasto, árboles y juegos
a seat on ropes or chains that moves back and forth
columpio: un asiento colgado que se mueve hacia adelante y hacia atrás
to hit something with your foot
patear: golpear algo con el pie
writeFor: tells what one person is doing (is + -ing)
a capital letter and a period
activities.correct: Nice describing! You named things in the picture and told what someone is doing.
activities.hint: Point to one person. What is that person doing? Write: The ___ is ___ing.
activities.support: Use I see ___. Then use The girl is ___ or The boy is ___.
activities.extension: Add a color word: The boy is kicking a red ball.

teacher.use: Picture description warm-up; works as a paper booklet item.
teacher.function: Inform — naming objects and actions with is + -ing.
teacher.lower: Students label 3 things in the picture first, then copy one frame.
teacher.onLevel: Expect 1–2 sentences that name objects and one action.
teacher.challenge: Ask for three sentences using also and and.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture; students write under it on lined paper.
teacher.prompt: What is one more thing happening in the park?

activities.title: Picture Story: The Seed
activities.skill: Narrate a three-picture story with first, next, last
activities.directions: Look at the three pictures. Write what happens first, next, and last. Use the words first, next, and last.
activities.prompt: Look at the three pictures. What happens to the seed? Tell the story in order.

picture.alt: Three panels: 1) a girl puts a seed in a pot of soil, 2) she waters the pot and a small sprout grows, 3) a tall yellow flower blooms in the pot and she smiles.

activities.responsePlaceholder: First, she ___. Next, she ___. Last, ___.

models.A: She puts a seed in a pot. The flower grows.
models.B: First, the girl puts a seed in a pot of soil. Then she waters the pot, and a little sprout comes up. Last, a tall yellow flower grows, and she is happy because her seed grew.
models.C: A girl grew a beautiful flower from one tiny seed. First, she pressed the seed into a pot of soil. Next, she watered it every day, and soon a small green sprout popped up. After a few weeks, a tall yellow flower opened in the sun. She smiled because her hard work helped the seed grow into a plant.

vocabulary: a tiny thing that grows into a plant
semilla: una cosa pequeña que crece y se convierte en planta
regar: darle agua a una planta
writeFor: action words like puts, waters, grows
activities.correct: Great story! You told the three parts in order with first, next, and last.
activities.hint: Look at picture 1 and write one sentence. Then do picture 2 and picture 3.
activities.support: One picture = one sentence. Start each sentence with first, next, or last.
activities.extension: Add how the girl feels at the end: She feels ___ because ___.

teacher.use: Picture-sequence narrative like the ACCESS booklet task.
teacher.function: Narrate — time-order words and past or present action verbs.
teacher.lower: Students say each panel aloud, then write with the three frames.
teacher.onLevel: Expect three ordered sentences with sequence words.
teacher.challenge: Add a feeling and a reason at the end.
teacher.noTech: Print the three panels; students write under each panel.
teacher.prompt: What does a seed need to grow?

activities.title: How to Make a Sandwich
activities.skill: Explain steps in order
activities.directions: Look at the pictures. Write how to make a sandwich. Write one sentence for each step.
activities.prompt: Look at the pictures. How do you make a sandwich? Write the steps.

picture.alt: Three steps to make a sandwich: 1) two slices of bread on a plate, 2) cheese and lettuce on one slice, 3) the finished sandwich cut in half.

activities.responsePlaceholder: First, put two slices of bread ___.

models.A: Put bread on a plate. Put cheese on the bread.
models.B: First, put two slices of bread on a plate. Then put cheese and lettuce on one slice. Last, put the bread on top and cut the sandwich in half so it is easy to eat.
models.C: Making a sandwich is easy if you follow three steps. First, place two slices of bread side by side on a clean plate. Next, add a slice of cheese and some green lettuce to one piece of bread. Finally, put the other slice on top and cut the sandwich in half. Now your lunch is ready to share or eat.

vocabulary: one part of how you do something
paso: una parte de cómo haces algo
rebanada: un pedazo delgado y plano
poner: colocar algo en un lugar
writeFor: the food words from the pictures
activities.correct: Clear steps! A friend could follow your directions to make a sandwich.
activities.hint: Start each step with an action word: Put, Add, Cut.
activities.support: Directions tell someone what to do. Use first, then, last.
activities.extension: Add one more step: what do you do after you make it?

teacher.use: Procedural writing from a picture sequence.
teacher.function: Explain — imperative verbs and sequence words.
teacher.lower: Act out each step with paper food, then write.
teacher.onLevel: Expect three imperative sentences in order.
teacher.challenge: Ask for a tip sentence: Be careful when you cut.
teacher.noTech: Print the steps; students write a list under the pictures.
teacher.prompt: Why do directions need to be in order?

activities.title: Pick a Class Pet
activities.skill: Give an opinion with a reason
activities.directions: Look at the two pictures. Which class pet is better, the fish or the hamster? Write your choice and one reason.
activities.prompt: Look at the two pictures. Which pet should our class get? Why?

picture.alt: Two choices for a class pet: a goldfish in a fish tank and a hamster in a cage with a wheel.

activities.responsePlaceholder: I think the ___ is better because ___.

models.A: I like the fish. It is pretty.
models.B: I think our class should get the hamster. I like it because it is soft and fun to watch. It runs on the wheel, so it is never boring.
models.C: Our class should get a goldfish as a class pet. First, a fish is quiet, so it will not bother us when we read or take tests. Also, it only needs a little food each day and a clean tank. A hamster is cute, but it can bite and needs more care. For these reasons, a goldfish is the best pet for our classroom.

vocabulary: an animal that lives with people
mascota: un animal que vive con las personas
more good than the other one
mejor: más bueno que el otro
porque: una palabra que dice por qué
activities.correct: Strong opinion! You made a choice and gave a reason with because.
activities.hint: First pick one pet. Then finish: because it is ___.
activities.support: An opinion tells what you think. Because tells why.
activities.extension: Add a second reason with also.

teacher.use: Opinion writing with a two-picture choice, like ACCESS.
teacher.lower: Students point to a picture and say I like ___ before writing.
teacher.onLevel: Expect a clear choice and one because reason.
teacher.challenge: Require two reasons and a closing sentence.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture; students circle a choice and write below.
teacher.prompt: What does each pet need to stay healthy?

activities.title: Write About the Shapes
activities.skill: Describe shapes with numbers and colors
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the shapes. Write how many of each shape you see. Use number words and color words.
activities.prompt: Look at the picture of the shapes. How many circles, triangles, and squares do you see?

picture.alt: Shapes on a table: three red circles, two blue triangles, and one yellow square.

activities.responsePlaceholder: I see three ___ circles. There are ___.

models.A: I see three red circles. I see one square.
models.B: I see three red circles on the table. There are two blue triangles too. There is only one yellow square, so there are six shapes in all.
models.C: There are six shapes on the table, and they come in three colors. First, I count three red circles in a row at the top. Next to them are two blue triangles with three sides each. Below the circles, there is one yellow square. There are more circles than any other shape.

vocabulary: triángulo: una figura con tres lados
a shape with four equal sides
cuadrado: una figura con cuatro lados iguales
activities.correct: Excellent math writing! You used numbers, colors, and shape names.
activities.hint: Count each shape. One shape = is. More than one = are, and add -s.
activities.support: Use There are for more than one. Use There is for one.
activities.extension: Write one more sentence: How many shapes are there in all?

teacher.use: Math-language description from a picture.
teacher.function: Inform — number words, plurals, there is / there are.
teacher.lower: Students count aloud and point; give the frames on a strip.
teacher.onLevel: Expect accurate counts with correct plural forms.
teacher.challenge: Ask students to compare: There are more ___ than ___.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture; students write sentences on lines.
teacher.prompt: How many sides do all of the shapes have together?

activities.title: What Is the Weather?
activities.skill: Describe weather and clothing
activities.directions: Look at the picture. Write about the weather. Tell what the boy is wearing.
activities.prompt: Look at the picture. What is the weather like? What is the boy wearing?

picture.alt: A rainy day: gray clouds, falling rain, and a boy in a yellow raincoat and boots holding a blue umbrella next to a puddle.

activities.responsePlaceholder: It is ___ today. The boy is wearing ___.

models.A: It is rainy. The boy has an umbrella.
models.B: It is a rainy day, and the sky is gray. The boy is wearing a yellow raincoat and boots. He holds a blue umbrella because he wants to stay dry.
models.C: Today the weather is cold, gray, and very rainy. Dark clouds cover the sky, and rain is falling everywhere. Because of the rain, the boy is wearing a yellow raincoat and rubber boots. He also holds a big blue umbrella over his head. He is ready to splash in the puddle and still stay dry.

vocabulary: what it is like outside, like rain or sun
tiempo (clima): cómo está afuera, como lluvia o sol
a cover you hold over you in the rain
paraguas: una cubierta que sostienes sobre ti cuando llueve
a jacket that keeps rain off
impermeable: una chaqueta que te protege de la lluvia
activities.correct: Good science writing! You described the weather and the clothes for it.
activities.hint: What falls from the clouds? What keeps the boy dry?
activities.support: Use It is ___ for weather. Use He is wearing ___ for clothes.
activities.extension: Write what the boy should NOT wear today and why.

teacher.use: Weather vocabulary in a describe-the-picture task.
teacher.function: Inform — weather adjectives and is wearing.
teacher.lower: Match word cards (rain, boots, umbrella) to the picture first.
teacher.onLevel: Expect a weather sentence and a clothing sentence.
teacher.challenge: Add a because sentence about why he wears boots.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture; students label it, then write.
teacher.prompt: What is the weather like today where you are?

activities.title: A Community Helper
activities.skill: Inform about a job in the community
activities.directions: Think of a person who helps your neighborhood. Write who the helper is and what the helper does.
activities.prompt: Who is a helper in your community? What does that helper do?
activities.responsePlaceholder: A ___ helps my community. The ___ ___.

models.A: A mail carrier helps my community. She brings letters.
models.B: A crossing guard helps my community. He works at the corner by my school. He stops the cars, so kids can cross the street safely.
models.C: Crossing guards are important helpers in my community. Every morning, Mr. Kofi stands at the busy corner near our school. He holds up a stop sign so cars wait while children cross. Also, he waves and says good morning to everyone. Because of him, students get to school safely every day.

vocabulary: the people and places where you live
comunidad: las personas y los lugares donde vives
ayudante: una persona que ayuda a otros
to bring something to a person
entregar: llevarle algo a una persona
activities.correct: Great informing! You named a helper and told how they help people.
activities.hint: Pick one helper from the word bank. Where do they work? What do they do?
activities.support: Use helps and works with -s: A nurse helps sick people.
activities.extension: Write a thank-you sentence to your helper.

teacher.use: Social studies informative writing without a picture prompt.
teacher.lower: Show photos or drawings of helpers from your school; students choose one.
teacher.onLevel: Expect 1–2 sentences naming a helper and an action.
teacher.challenge: Ask for a reason the job is important.
teacher.noTech: Students write and draw the helper on paper.
teacher.prompt: Who helps at our school every day?

activities.title: Fix the Action Words
activities.skill: Choose the correct verb form
activities.directions: Read the sentences. Choose the word that fits each blank.
activities.prompt: Choose the right word for each blank.

segments.text: to school every day. Her brothers

vocabulary: an action word, like run or eat
verbo: una palabra de acción, como correr o comer
a boy in your family with the same parents
hermano: un niño de tu familia con los mismos padres
frames: One person walks. Two people walk.
writeFor: is for one, are for more than one
activities.correct: Correct! One person gets -s (walks). More than one person gets no -s (walk).
activities.hint: Ask: Is it one person or more than one person?
activities.support: Maya = one person → walks, is. Her brothers = more than one → walk, are.
activities.extension: Write a sentence about your family using walk or walks.

teacher.use: Grammar mini-lesson on subject-verb agreement.
teacher.lower: Hold up one finger or two fingers for each subject before choosing.
teacher.onLevel: Students complete all three blanks independently.
teacher.challenge: Students rewrite the sentences about themselves (I walk...).
teacher.noTech: Print and circle the right word.
teacher.prompt: How do you know when to add -s to a verb?

activities.title: Build a Paragraph: A Card for Grandma
activities.skill: Put sentences in order
activities.directions: Put the sentences in order to make a short paragraph. Use the buttons to move each sentence.
activities.prompt: Put the sentences in the right order.

items.text: Then, I drew a big red heart on the front.
Last, I wrote I love you inside the card.
Today I made a card for my grandma.
First, I folded a piece of paper in half.

vocabulary: folded paper with a message for someone
tarjeta: papel doblado con un mensaje para alguien
to bend paper so one part covers the other
doblar: plegar el papel para que una parte cubra la otra
in the middle part of something
adentro: en la parte de en medio de algo
frames: First, I ___. Then, I ___. Last, I ___.
writeFor: the last sentence finishes the story
activities.correct: Correct! The paragraph starts with the topic, then follows first, then, and last.
activities.hint: Which sentence tells what the whole paragraph is about? Put it first.
activities.support: Look for the order words: first, then, last.
activities.extension: Write one more sentence: what did Grandma say?

teacher.use: Paragraph structure practice before writing a story.
teacher.function: Narrate — topic sentence and sequence words.
teacher.lower: Use sentence strips students can move on the desk.
teacher.onLevel: Students order on screen.
teacher.challenge: Students write their own four-sentence paragraph about making something.
teacher.noTech: Cut the sentences into strips and order them.
teacher.prompt: What words helped you find the order?

activities.title: Pick the Best Sentence
activities.skill: Choose a complete, correct sentence
activities.directions: Read the four sentences. Choose the one that is complete and written correctly.
activities.prompt: Which sentence is complete and correct?

options.text: The dog run in the park.
the dog runs in the park
The dog runs in the park.

vocabulary: a group of words that tells a complete idea
oración: un grupo de palabras que dice una idea completa
a big letter, like A or T
letra mayúscula: una letra grande, como A o T
the dot at the end of a sentence
punto: la marca al final de una oración
frames: A sentence starts with a ___ and ends with a ___.
writeFor: a capital letter at the start
words in an order that makes sense
activities.correct: Yes! It starts with a capital letter, ends with a period, and the words are in order.
activities.hint: Check three things: capital letter, period, and words that make sense.
activities.support: One dog runs. A sentence needs a capital letter and a period.
activities.extension: Write your own sentence about an animal. Check the three things.

teacher.use: Quick check of sentence conventions.
teacher.function: Capitalization, end punctuation, and word order.
teacher.lower: Read each choice aloud and check one rule at a time.
teacher.onLevel: Students choose and explain one error in another choice.
teacher.challenge: Students fix all three wrong sentences.
teacher.noTech: Print and circle; fix the others in pencil.
teacher.prompt: What is wrong with each of the other sentences?

activities.title: Worksheet — My Weekend Story
activities.skill: Printable story plan and writing lines
activities.directions: Print this page. Draw in the boxes, then write one sentence for each part of your weekend.
vocabulary: fin de semana: sábado y domingo
to make a picture with a pencil or crayon
dibujar: hacer una imagen con lápiz o crayón
activities.correct: Your weekend story has three parts in order. Well done!
activities.hint: Draw first. Then use your drawing to write each sentence.
activities.support: Use past words: play → played, go → went, eat → ate.
activities.extension: Add how you felt: I felt ___ because ___.

teacher.use: Printable narrative practice matching the handwritten ACCESS booklet.
teacher.lower: Students draw and dictate; teacher writes, student copies.
teacher.onLevel: Expect three sentences in order.
teacher.challenge: Expect five sentences with a feeling ending.
teacher.noTech: This item is paper-first.
teacher.prompt: What was the best part of your weekend?

activities.title: Worksheet — My Favorite Food
activities.skill: Printable opinion writing
activities.directions: Print this page. Write about your favorite food and tell why you like it.

sheet.heading: Part 1 — Plan
items: How it tastes: sweet / salty / spicy / ______ (circle)

vocabulary: the one you like the most
favorito: el que más te gusta
activities.correct: You shared an opinion and a reason. Nice writing!
activities.hint: Think of how the food tastes or who makes it for you.
activities.support: Use the frames on the sheet line by line.
activities.extension: Add a second reason with also.

teacher.use: Printable opinion practice on a familiar topic.
teacher.lower: Allow a drawing plus one frame.
teacher.onLevel: Expect an opinion, reason, and closing.
teacher.challenge: Ask for two reasons and a closing that restates the opinion.
teacher.noTech: This item is paper-first.
teacher.prompt: Who makes your favorite food?

B.studentGoal: I can write 3–4 connected sentences using because, first, and then.

info.headline: Write connected sentences that tell, explain, and give reasons
info.summary: Growing writers connect 3–4 sentences with linking words like because, so, but, first, and then. They narrate a picture story, explain a process in science or math, describe a community place, and give an opinion with two reasons.
canDo: I can write a story with a beginning, middle, and end.
I can explain steps or a process in order.
I can give an opinion with two reasons.
I can join ideas with because, so, and but.

categories.title: Write About Pictures
categories.desc: Tell a picture story, explain a diagram, and describe a scene.

categories.title: Explain and Give Opinions
categories.desc: Explain math and school routines, describe a character, and support an opinion.

categories.title: Connect Your Ideas
categories.desc: Choose linking words, sort facts and opinions, and join sentences.

categories.title: Paper Practice
categories.desc: Printable story maps and opinion planners.

activities.title: Picture Story: The Lost Backpack
activities.skill: Narrate a story with time words and feelings
activities.directions: Look at the three pictures. Write a story of 3–4 sentences. Tell what happens in each picture and how the characters feel.
activities.prompt: Look at the three pictures. What happens to the green backpack? Write the story.

picture.alt: Three panels: 1) a boy walks away from a school bus and leaves his green backpack on the seat, 2) a girl on the bus finds the green backpack, 3) the girl gives the backpack back to the boy at school and they both smile.

activities.responsePlaceholder: First, the boy ___. Then, ___. At the end, ___.

models.A: The boy left his backpack. The girl gave it back.
models.B: First, a boy got off the bus, but he forgot his green backpack. Then, a girl on the bus found it on the seat. At the end, she gave it back to him at school, and he was happy because his homework was inside.
models.C: One morning, Daniel learned how much a kind friend can help. First, he jumped off the school bus in a hurry and left his green backpack on the seat. Soon after, Amina saw the backpack and picked it up carefully. When she got to school, she ran to the door and handed it to Daniel. He smiled and said thank you, because all of his homework was safe.

vocabulary: to see something you were looking for
encontrar: ver algo que estabas buscando
writeFor: what happens in all three pictures
time words: first, then, at the end
activities.correct: Wonderful story! Your events are in order and you showed how the characters feel.
activities.hint: Write one sentence for each picture, then add a feeling sentence.
activities.support: Past tense helps a story: leave → left, find → found, give → gave.
activities.extension: Give the characters names and add something they say.

teacher.use: Three-panel narrative, as on the ACCESS writing test.
teacher.function: Narrate — past tense, time order, feelings.
teacher.lower: Oral rehearsal: students tell the story to a partner before writing.
teacher.onLevel: Expect 3–4 connected sentences covering all panels.
teacher.challenge: Require dialogue and a lesson at the end.
teacher.noTech: Print the panels; students write under them.
teacher.prompt: What would you do if you found a friend's backpack?

activities.title: Explain the Water Cycle
activities.skill: Explain a science process in order
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the water cycle. Write 3–4 sentences that explain how water moves. Use sequence words.
activities.prompt: Look at the picture of the water cycle. How does water move from the ocean to the sky and back?

picture.alt: The water cycle: the sun warms the ocean, water rises as vapor, clouds form, rain falls on a mountain, and a river flows back to the ocean.

activities.responsePlaceholder: First, the sun warms ___. Then, ___.

models.A: The sun makes the water go up. Rain comes down.
models.B: First, the sun warms the water in the ocean. Then, the water evaporates and goes up to make clouds. After that, rain falls on the mountain, and a river carries the water back to the ocean.
models.C: The water cycle shows how water moves around the Earth again and again. First, the sun heats the ocean, so some water evaporates into the air as vapor. Next, the vapor cools high in the sky and forms clouds. When the clouds get heavy, rain falls on the mountains. Finally, rivers carry the water back to the ocean, and the cycle starts again.

vocabulary: when water turns into a gas and goes up into the air
evaporarse: cuando el agua se convierte en gas y sube al aire
tiny drops of water floating in the sky
nube: gotas pequeñas de agua que flotan en el cielo
something that happens again and again in a circle
ciclo: algo que pasa una y otra vez en círculo
writeFor: how the water gets back to the ocean
activities.correct: Excellent science explanation! You showed each step and how the cycle starts again.
activities.hint: Follow the arrows in the picture with your finger. Write one sentence for each arrow.
activities.support: Sun warms water → water goes up → clouds → rain → river → ocean.
activities.extension: Explain why the water cycle never stops.

teacher.use: Science explanation from a labeled-free diagram.
teacher.function: Explain — cause and sequence in a process.
teacher.lower: Give students cards for each stage to order before writing.
teacher.onLevel: Expect 3–4 sentences in correct order with key terms.
teacher.challenge: Ask for cause words: because, so, when.
teacher.noTech: Print the diagram; students add arrows and write.
teacher.prompt: Where does rain water go after it falls?

activities.title: Choose a Field Trip
activities.skill: Write an opinion with two reasons
activities.directions: Look at the two pictures. Should your class visit the museum or the farm? Write your opinion with two reasons.
activities.prompt: Look at the two pictures. Which field trip should your class take? Give two reasons.

picture.alt: Two field trip choices: a museum with a dinosaur skeleton and a farm with a red barn, a cow, and apple trees.

activities.responsePlaceholder: Our class should visit the ___. One reason is ___.

models.A: We should go to the farm. I like cows.
models.B: I think our class should visit the farm. One reason is that we can see real animals like cows. Also, we can pick apples from the trees, so it will be fun and healthy.
models.C: Our class should take a field trip to the museum. First of all, we could see a real dinosaur skeleton and learn how big these animals were. In addition, a museum has guides who explain science and history to students. The farm sounds fun, but we can see animals at many places. For these reasons, the museum is the best choice for our class.

vocabulary: a building where people look at important objects
museo: un edificio donde la gente mira objetos importantes
a class visit to a place outside school
excursión: una visita de la clase a un lugar fuera de la escuela
writeFor: linking words: because, also, another reason
activities.correct: Convincing! You gave a clear opinion and backed it up with two reasons.
activities.hint: Pick one place. Then think: What can we learn there? What can we do there?
activities.support: Opinion → Reason 1 → Reason 2. Use because and also.
activities.extension: Add a closing sentence that tells your opinion again.

teacher.use: Opinion writing from a picture choice.
teacher.function: Argue — opinion with two reasons and linking words.
teacher.lower: Students fill a T-chart of what they see in each picture first.
teacher.onLevel: Expect opinion + two reasons in 3–4 sentences.
teacher.challenge: Ask students to say why the other place is less good.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture; students circle a choice and write.
teacher.prompt: Which reason do you think is strongest?

activities.title: Describe the Community Market
activities.skill: Describe a community place with details
activities.directions: Look at the picture. Write 3–4 sentences that describe the community market. Tell what people sell and what people do.
activities.prompt: Look at the picture of the market. What do the stands sell? What are the people doing?

picture.alt: A busy community market with two stands under striped roofs, one selling fruit and one selling vegetables, a seller, and a mother and child carrying a shopping bag.

activities.responsePlaceholder: At the market, I see ___. One stand sells ___.

models.A: I see a market. They sell fruit.
models.B: The community market is busy today. One stand sells apples, oranges, and bananas, and the other stand sells carrots and lettuce. A mother and her child are shopping because they need food for dinner.
models.C: On a sunny day, the community market is full of fresh food. On the left, a friendly seller stands behind a table of red apples, oranges, and bananas. Next to it, a stand with a green striped roof sells carrots, lettuce, and tomatoes. Meanwhile, a mother and her child carry a shopping bag full of vegetables. Markets like this help families buy fresh food close to home.

vocabulary: a place where people buy and sell things

vendedor: una persona que vende cosas

activities.correct: Vivid describing! A reader can picture the busy market from your words.
activities.hint: Start with the stands: what is on each one? Then write about the people.
activities.support: Use and to connect: One stand sells fruit, and the other sells vegetables.
activities.extension: Tell why markets are important for a community.

teacher.use: Social studies scene description (goods, buyers, sellers).
teacher.function: Inform — descriptive detail and compound sentences.
teacher.lower: Label goods and people on the picture before writing.
teacher.onLevel: Expect 3–4 sentences naming goods and actions.

teacher.prompt: What do people in your neighborhood buy at a market?

activities.title: Explain How You Solved It
activities.skill: Explain math steps in writing
activities.directions: Solve the word problem. Then write 3–4 sentences that explain how you solved it.
activities.prompt: Amir has 3 bags. Each bag has 4 apples. How many apples does Amir have in all? Explain how you know.
activities.responsePlaceholder: First, I ___. Then, I ___. So, Amir has ___ apples.

models.A: Amir has 12 apples. I did 3 times 4.
models.B: First, I saw that Amir has 3 equal groups of apples. Then, I multiplied 3 times 4 because each bag has 4 apples. So, Amir has 12 apples in all.
models.C: Amir has 12 apples in all, and I solved it with multiplication. First, I noticed the problem has 3 bags with the same number of apples in each one. Because these are equal groups, I wrote 3 × 4. Then, I checked by adding 4 + 4 + 4, which also equals 12. Both strategies show that Amir has 12 apples.

vocabulary: groups that have the same number
grupos iguales: grupos que tienen el mismo número
writeFor: math words: equal groups, multiply, total
activities.correct: Clear math explanation! You told your steps and why they work.
activities.hint: How many bags? How many apples in each bag? What operation joins equal groups?
activities.support: 3 bags with 4 in each bag = 3 × 4. You can also add 4 + 4 + 4.
activities.extension: Show a second way to solve it and explain that way too.

teacher.use: Math writing — explaining a strategy.
teacher.function: Explain — sequence and cause in math reasoning.
teacher.lower: Let students draw the bags and apples first.
teacher.onLevel: Expect correct answer (12) and 3 sentences of steps.
teacher.challenge: Ask for two strategies and a check.
teacher.noTech: Work on paper with a drawing box.
teacher.prompt: How could you check your answer?

activities.title: Describe a Story Character
activities.skill: Describe a character with evidence
activities.directions: Think about the tortoise in the fable The Tortoise and the Hare. Write 3–4 sentences that describe the tortoise and tell what it did.
activities.prompt: What is the tortoise like in The Tortoise and the Hare? Use what the tortoise did to show it.
activities.responsePlaceholder: The tortoise is ___. I know this because ___.

models.A: The tortoise is slow. It wins the race.
models.B: The tortoise is slow, but it is patient. I know this because it kept walking while the hare took a nap. In the end, the tortoise won the race, so the lesson is to never give up.
models.C: The tortoise in the fable is patient and determined. Even though it walked very slowly, it never stopped moving toward the finish line. Meanwhile, the hare was so sure of winning that it took a nap under a tree. Because the tortoise kept going, it crossed the finish line first. This character teaches us that steady work can beat fast but careless work.

vocabulary: a person or animal in a story
personaje: una persona o un animal en un cuento
able to wait and keep going calmly
paciente: que puede esperar y seguir con calma
a short story that teaches a lesson
fábula: un cuento corto que enseña una lección
activities.correct: Thoughtful writing! You described the tortoise and used the story as evidence.
activities.hint: What word describes the tortoise? What did it do in the race?
activities.support: Trait + because + what the character did. Example: The tortoise is patient because it kept walking.
activities.extension: Compare the tortoise and the hare in one more sentence.

teacher.use: Literary response with a well-known fable (read it aloud first if needed).
teacher.function: Inform — trait words with text evidence.
teacher.lower: Read the fable aloud with pictures; list traits as a class.
teacher.onLevel: Expect a trait, evidence, and lesson.
teacher.challenge: Add a comparison with the hare using but or while.
teacher.noTech: Students write on paper after a read-aloud.
teacher.prompt: What lesson does this fable teach?

activities.title: Help a New Student
activities.skill: Explain a school routine
activities.directions: A new student is joining your class. Write 3–4 sentences that explain how to get lunch in the cafeteria.
activities.prompt: How do you get lunch in our cafeteria? Explain the steps to a new student.
activities.responsePlaceholder: First, you line up ___. Next, ___.

models.A: You get a tray. You get your food.
models.B: First, you line up with your class at the cafeteria door. Next, you take a tray and choose your food and milk. After that, you sit at our class table, and you clean up before recess.
models.C: Getting lunch in our cafeteria is easy once you know the steps. First, you line up quietly with our class by the cafeteria door. Next, you take a tray, pick a main dish, and grab a fruit and a milk. After you pay or say your lunch number, you sit at the table with our class sign. Finally, remember to throw away your trash so the table is clean for the next class.

vocabulary: the room where students eat lunch
cafetería: el salón donde los estudiantes almuerzan
a flat thing you carry food on
bandeja: una cosa plana para cargar comida
to stand one behind the other
hacer fila: pararse uno detrás del otro
writeFor: one helpful tip for the new student
activities.correct: Very helpful! A new student could follow your steps on the first day.
activities.hint: Picture yourself walking into the cafeteria. What do you do first?
activities.support: Use you + action: First, you line up. Next, you take a tray.
activities.extension: Add a friendly sentence to welcome the new student.

teacher.use: Procedural writing about a real school routine.
teacher.lower: Walk through the routine orally with gestures.
teacher.onLevel: Expect 3–4 ordered steps with sequence words.
teacher.challenge: Add a tip with because or so.
teacher.noTech: Write on paper as a welcome note.
teacher.prompt: What else should a new student know about our school?

activities.title: Choose the Linking Words
activities.skill: Use because, so, but, then to connect ideas
activities.directions: Read the paragraph about a science experiment. Choose the linking word that makes sense in each blank.
activities.prompt: Choose the best linking word for each blank.

segments.text: Our class did an ice experiment.
, we put one ice cube in the sun and one in the shade. The ice in the sun melted faster
the sun is warm. The shade was cool,
that ice melted slowly. We predicted both would melt,
we did not know which one would be first.

vocabulary: a test to find out something in science
experimento: una prueba para descubrir algo en ciencias
to change from solid to liquid
derretirse: cambiar de sólido a líquido
predecir: adivinar lo que va a pasar
activities.correct: Correct! Each linking word shows how the ideas connect: order, reason, result, or difference.
activities.hint: Read the whole sentence. Is the second part a reason, a result, or something different?
activities.support: because = why · so = what happened next as a result · but = a surprise or difference
activities.extension: Write your own sentence about ice using so.

teacher.use: Linking-word practice inside a science context.
teacher.function: Explain — cohesive devices for cause, result, contrast.
teacher.lower: Pre-teach each linking word with a hand signal.
teacher.onLevel: Students complete independently and read the paragraph aloud.
teacher.challenge: Students rewrite the paragraph with different linking words.
teacher.noTech: Print and circle.
teacher.prompt: Which linking word was hardest to choose? Why?

activities.title: Fact or Opinion?
activities.skill: Tell facts from opinions
activities.directions: Read each sentence about the ocean. Sort it: is it a Fact or an Opinion? Use the buttons.
activities.prompt: Sort each sentence into Fact or Opinion.

items.text: Ocean water is salty.
The ocean is the most beautiful place in the world.
Whales live in the ocean.
I think swimming in the ocean is better than swimming in a pool.
The ocean covers most of the Earth.
Everyone should visit the ocean every summer.

vocabulary: something that is true and can be checked
hecho: algo que es verdad y se puede comprobar
opinión: lo que alguien piensa o siente
a very large body of salt water
océano: una gran cantidad de agua salada
writeFor: opinions use feeling words like best or beautiful
activities.correct: Great sorting! Facts can be checked; opinions tell what someone thinks.
activities.hint: Could you check it in a book? Then it is a fact. Is it a feeling? Then it is an opinion.
activities.support: Opinion clue words: best, worst, beautiful, boring, I think, should.
activities.extension: Write one fact and one opinion about your school.

teacher.use: Prepares students to support opinions with facts.
teacher.function: Classify statements as fact or opinion.
teacher.lower: Highlight clue words (best, I think) before sorting.
teacher.onLevel: Students sort and explain one choice.
teacher.challenge: Students turn each opinion into a fact sentence.
teacher.noTech: Cut and sort sentence strips into two columns.
teacher.prompt: Why do opinion paragraphs need facts too?

activities.title: Join Two Ideas
activities.skill: Choose the best way to combine sentences
activities.directions: Read the two short sentences. Choose the sentence that joins them in the clearest way.
activities.prompt: It was raining. We played inside. Which sentence joins these ideas best?

options.text: It was raining but we played inside.
It was raining because we played inside.
It was raining, so we played inside.

vocabulary: adentro: en un edificio, no afuera
resultado: lo que pasa por algo
writeFor: the joined sentence keeps the meaning
activities.correct: Yes! It was raining, so we played inside — so shows the result of the rain.
activities.hint: What happened first? What happened as a result?
activities.support: Rain is the reason. Playing inside is the result. A result word is so.
activities.extension: Join these: I was hungry. I ate an apple.

teacher.use: Sentence combining to build more fluent writing.
teacher.lower: Read each choice aloud and ask: does this make sense?
teacher.onLevel: Students choose and explain why the others are weaker.
teacher.challenge: Students write three combined sentences of their own.
teacher.noTech: Print and circle.
teacher.prompt: Why does because not work in choice b?

activities.title: Worksheet — Beginning, Middle, End Story Map
activities.skill: Printable story planner
activities.directions: Print this page. Plan a story about a time you helped someone. Then write your story on the lines.

something that is wrong or hard

something that shows what you mean

teacher.lower: Accept words or drawings in each section.
teacher.onLevel: Expect a 4-sentence paragraph from the plan.

C.studentGoal: I can write a paragraph with a topic sentence, details, transitions, and a closing.

info.headline: Write organized paragraphs with details, transitions, and closings

canDo: I can write a paragraph with a topic sentence, details, and a closing.
I can use facts and numbers from a graph or table in my writing.
I can use transitions like in addition, as a result, and in conclusion.
I can choose precise words to make my writing clear.

categories.title: Tell Stories

activities.title: Picture Story: Clean-Up Day
activities.skill: Narrate a developed story with transitions and a closing
activities.directions: Look at the three pictures. Write a story paragraph with a beginning, middle, and end. Use transitions and describe how the characters feel.
activities.prompt: Look at the three pictures. How did the neighbors change their park? Write the story.

picture.alt: Three panels: 1) a park with trash on the grass, 2) neighbors wearing gloves pick up the trash and put it in bags, 3) the clean park has new flowers and the neighbors smile.

activities.responsePlaceholder: One day, Lucía noticed ___. Soon, ___.

models.A: The park had trash. People cleaned it.
models.B: First, the park was dirty, and there was trash on the grass. Then, the neighbors put on gloves and picked up the trash. At the end, the park was clean, and they were happy because they planted flowers.
models.C: One Saturday, Lucía walked to her favorite park and saw litter all over the grass. She felt upset, so she asked her neighbors to help clean it. Soon, everyone put on gloves and filled big bags with cans, bottles, and wrappers. By the end of the day, they had also planted bright pink flowers near the bench. The neighbors smiled at their clean park because they had worked together as a community.

vocabulary: basura tirada: desechos dejados en el suelo
a person who lives near you
vecino: una persona que vive cerca de ti
ser voluntario: ayudar sin recibir pago
frames: By the end of the day, ___.
wordBank: by the end of the day
writeFor: a beginning that sets the scene
events from all three pictures with transitions
activities.correct: A complete, well-told story! Your transitions moved the reader smoothly from problem to solution.
activities.hint: Plan: Problem (picture 1) → Action (picture 2) → Result (picture 3). Add one feeling for each.
activities.support: Use transitions: one day, soon, together, by the end of the day.
activities.extension: Add dialogue: what did one neighbor say?

teacher.use: Three-panel narrative at the expanding level.
teacher.lower: Give a story map with sentence starters for each panel.
teacher.onLevel: Expect a paragraph of 5+ sentences covering all panels.
teacher.challenge: Require dialogue and a theme statement.
teacher.noTech: Print the panels; write a paragraph beneath.
teacher.prompt: How can kids help their community?

activities.title: How to Make a Bird Feeder
activities.skill: Explain a procedure with precise verbs and transitions
activities.directions: Look at the pictures. Write a paragraph that explains how to make a bird feeder. Include a topic sentence, the steps, and a closing.
activities.prompt: Look at the pictures. How do you make a pinecone bird feeder? Explain the steps.

picture.alt: Three steps to make a bird feeder: 1) spread sunflower butter on a pinecone, 2) roll the pinecone in birdseed on a plate, 3) hang the pinecone on a tree branch where a bird eats.

activities.responsePlaceholder: You can make a bird feeder with a pinecone. To begin, ___.

models.A: Put butter on a pinecone. Hang it on a tree.
models.B: First, spread sunflower butter on a pinecone. Then, roll the pinecone in birdseed on a plate. Last, hang it on a tree branch so the birds can eat.
models.C: You can make a simple bird feeder with a pinecone and a few materials. To begin, spread sunflower butter all over the pinecone so the seeds will stick. Next, roll the sticky pinecone in a plate of birdseed until it is covered. Finally, tie a string to the top and hang it on a high tree branch. Soon, hungry birds will visit your feeder for a snack.

vocabulary: to cover a surface with a thin layer
untar: cubrir una superficie con una capa delgada
alpiste: semillas pequeñas que comen los pájaros
to attach something high so it does not touch the ground
colgar: sujetar algo en alto para que no toque el suelo
frames: You can make a bird feeder with ___.
writeFor: steps with precise verbs: spread, roll, hang
activities.correct: Clear and precise! Your verbs and transitions make the steps easy to follow.
activities.hint: Use the exact action in each picture: spread, roll, hang.
activities.support: Topic sentence → step 1 → step 2 → step 3 → closing about the birds.
activities.extension: Add a materials list sentence at the start.

teacher.use: Procedural paragraph from a picture sequence.
teacher.lower: Students list materials and verbs before writing.
teacher.onLevel: Expect a 5-sentence paragraph with topic and closing.
teacher.challenge: Explain why each step matters (why sticky butter, why hang high).
teacher.noTech: Print the steps and write beneath.
teacher.prompt: Why should the feeder hang high in a tree?

activities.title: Write About the Bean Plant Data
activities.skill: Inform using data from a bar graph
activities.directions: Use the bar graph to write a paragraph about how the bean plant grew. Include numbers from the graph and compare the weeks.
activities.prompt: Use the bar graph. How did the bean plant change over four weeks?
activities.responsePlaceholder: The graph shows ___. In week 1, ___.

models.A: The plant grew. It was 14 cm.
models.B: The graph shows how tall a bean plant grew. In week 1, it was 2 centimeters tall. Then it grew every week, and in week 4 it was 14 centimeters tall.
models.C: The bar graph shows that the bean plant grew taller every week for four weeks. In week 1, the plant was only 2 centimeters tall. By week 3, it had grown to 9 centimeters. The biggest change happened between week 3 and week 4, when it grew 5 more centimeters. Overall, the plant increased by 12 centimeters, so it grew faster as it got older.

vocabulary: altura: qué tan alto es algo
a small unit for measuring length
centímetro: una unidad pequeña para medir longitud
aumentar: hacerse más grande en número
frames: In week 1, the plant was ___ cm tall.
Between week ___ and week ___, it grew ___ cm.
writeFor: at least two numbers from the graph
a comparison and an overall closing
activities.correct: Excellent data writing! You used numbers and comparisons to explain the trend.
activities.hint: Read each bar. Then subtract to find how much the plant grew between weeks.
activities.support: Week 1 = 2 cm, week 2 = 5 cm, week 3 = 9 cm, week 4 = 14 cm.
activities.extension: Predict how tall the plant will be in week 5 and explain why.

teacher.use: Math/science data writing with an app-drawn bar graph.
teacher.lower: Students write each bar value on a sticky note first.
teacher.onLevel: Expect topic, two data points, comparison, closing.
teacher.challenge: Calculate the total growth and the biggest weekly change.
teacher.noTech: Copy the graph on paper and write beneath.
teacher.prompt: When did the plant grow the most?

activities.title: Should Recess Be Longer?
activities.skill: Write an opinion paragraph with reasons and a closing
activities.directions: Write an opinion paragraph: Should your school have a longer recess? Include a topic sentence, two reasons with details, a transition, and a closing.
activities.prompt: Should our school have a longer recess? Write your opinion and support it with reasons.
activities.responsePlaceholder: In my opinion, ___. First, ___.

models.A: Recess should be longer. I like to play.
models.B: I think recess should be longer because kids need to move. When we run and play, we feel better. Then we can focus in class, so we learn more.
models.C: In my opinion, our school should have a longer recess. First, children need exercise to stay healthy, and playing tag or soccer keeps our bodies strong. In addition, a break helps our brains rest, so we can focus better when we return to class. Some people think a longer recess means less learning time, but students who rest learn faster. In conclusion, a longer recess would make our school healthier and smarter.

vocabulary: free time to play during the school day
recreo: tiempo libre para jugar durante el día escolar
words that start the last sentence
en conclusión: palabras que empiezan la última oración
writeFor: a clear opinion in the topic sentence
transitions and a closing that restates the opinion
activities.correct: Persuasive and organized! Your reasons, details, and closing work together.
activities.hint: Plan with O-R-E-O before writing: opinion, reasons, examples, opinion again.
activities.support: Make each reason stronger with a detail or example.
activities.extension: Answer the other side: what would a teacher who disagrees say?

teacher.use: Opinion paragraph without picture support.
teacher.lower: Provide the OREO organizer and a reasons word bank.
teacher.onLevel: Expect topic, two supported reasons, closing.
teacher.challenge: Require a counterargument and response.
teacher.noTech: Write on paper after planning on the organizer.
teacher.prompt: What is the strongest reason on each side?

activities.title: Compare Two Habitats
activities.skill: Compare and contrast using data from a table
activities.directions: Read the table. Write a paragraph that compares the desert and the rainforest. Tell how they are alike and how they are different.
activities.prompt: Use the table to compare the desert and the rainforest. How are they alike and different?
activities.responsePlaceholder: The desert and the rainforest are both ___. However, ___.

models.A: The desert is dry. The rainforest has rain.
models.B: The desert and the rainforest are both habitats for animals. The desert is very dry, but the rainforest gets a lot of rain. Also, a camel lives in the desert, while a monkey lives in the rainforest.
models.C: The desert and the rainforest are both habitats, but they are very different places to live. The biggest difference is rain, because the desert gets less than 25 centimeters a year while the rainforest gets more than 200. In addition, the desert has hot days and cold nights, but the rainforest stays warm all year. As a result, the desert has only a few plants like cactus, and the rainforest is full of tall trees. In summary, rain and temperature shape which plants and animals live in each habitat.

vocabulary: the natural home of a plant or animal
hábitat: el hogar natural de una planta o un animal
a very dry place with little rain
desierto: un lugar muy seco con poca lluvia
a warm forest with lots of rain
selva tropical: un bosque cálido con mucha lluvia
frames: The desert and the rainforest are both ___.
However, the desert ___, while the rainforest ___.
writeFor: two differences with facts from the table
compare words and a summary closing
activities.correct: Strong comparison! You used facts from the table and compare-contrast words.
activities.hint: Find one row where they are the same. Then find two rows where they are different.
activities.support: Alike: both. Different: however, while, on the other hand.
activities.extension: Explain how one animal is adapted to its habitat.

teacher.use: Science compare/contrast paragraph using a data table.
teacher.lower: Students fill a Venn diagram from the table before writing.
teacher.onLevel: Expect a similarity, two differences, closing.
teacher.challenge: Add an explanation of animal adaptation.
teacher.noTech: Copy the table; use a Venn diagram on paper.
teacher.prompt: Which habitat would be harder for a plant? Why?

activities.title: A Person Who Made a Difference

activities.title: Finish the Mystery Story

activities.prompt: Story beginning: Noor opened her lunchbox and gasped. Her lunch was gone! In its place was a tiny folded note with a drawing of a tree. What happens next?
activities.responsePlaceholder: Noor unfolded the note. It said ___.

models.A: Noor found her lunch. Her friend had it.
models.B: Noor read the note and ran outside to the big tree. Then she found her lunch on a picnic table. Her friends were there, and they said surprise because it was her birthday.
models.C: Noor unfolded the note and saw a drawing of the old oak tree by the playground. She grabbed her jacket and hurried outside to follow the clue. Under the tree, she found a basket with her lunch and a second note that said, "Look up!" Suddenly, her classmates jumped out from behind the tree and shouted, "Happy birthday, Noor!" At last, the mystery was solved, and it was the best lunch she ever had.

activities.hint: What did the note say? Where did Noor go? Who took the lunch?
activities.support: Use story transitions: suddenly, after that, at last.
activities.extension: Write the story from the point of view of the person who wrote the note.

teacher.use: Narrative continuation (language arts).
teacher.lower: Brainstorm three possible endings as a class first.
teacher.onLevel: Expect 5+ sentences with a clear resolution.
teacher.challenge: Require dialogue punctuation and a twist.
teacher.noTech: Write the ending on paper.
teacher.prompt: How did you make your ending surprising?

activities.title: Build an Informational Paragraph: Bees
activities.skill: Order a paragraph with a topic sentence, details, and closing
activities.directions: Put the sentences in order to build a strong informational paragraph about bees.
activities.prompt: Put the sentences in order to make the paragraph.

items.text: As a result, those flowers can make seeds and fruit.
In conclusion, bees help give us many of the foods we eat.
Bees are small insects that do a very important job.
They also carry pollen from one flower to another.
First, bees visit flowers to drink sweet nectar.

vocabulary: polen: polvo amarillo dentro de las flores
colmena: la casa donde viven las abejas
frames: The topic sentence is ___ because it ___.
activities.correct: Correct! Topic sentence, details linked by transitions, then the closing.
activities.hint: Find the sentence that tells the big idea. Find the one that starts with In conclusion.
activities.support: Transitions show order: first → also → as a result → in conclusion.
activities.extension: Write one more detail sentence about bees using also.

teacher.use: Model of a complete informational paragraph.
teacher.lower: Color-code the topic and closing sentences first.
teacher.onLevel: Students order on screen and name each sentence's job.
teacher.challenge: Students write a parallel paragraph about another insect.
teacher.noTech: Order printed strips on the desk.
teacher.prompt: Which words helped you find the order?

activities.title: Topic Sentence, Detail, or Closing?
activities.skill: Identify the job of each sentence
activities.directions: These sentences come from a paragraph about the public library. Sort each one: Topic Sentence, Detail, or Closing.
activities.prompt: Sort each sentence by its job in the paragraph.

items.text: Kids can join a free reading club every summer.
The public library is one of the most useful places in our community.
Families can borrow books, movies, and games for free.
For these reasons, everyone should get a library card.
The library also has computers that anyone can use.

vocabulary: the sentence that tells the main idea
oración principal: la oración que dice la idea principal
a fact or example that supports the main idea
detalle: un dato o ejemplo que apoya la idea principal
the last sentence that wraps up the paragraph
cierre: la última oración que termina el párrafo
frames: This is a detail because it ___.
This is the closing because it ___.
writeFor: one topic sentence with the main idea
activities.correct: Great work! You found the main idea, the supporting details, and the wrap-up.
activities.hint: Which sentence is the biggest idea? Which sentence sounds like an ending?
activities.support: Closings often start with In conclusion, That is why, or For these reasons.
activities.extension: Write a new detail sentence for this paragraph.

teacher.use: Paragraph-structure analysis with a community-place topic.
teacher.lower: Sort topic and closing first, then the details.
teacher.onLevel: Students sort and justify one choice.
teacher.challenge: Students rewrite the topic sentence in a more interesting way.
teacher.noTech: Cut and sort sentence strips.
teacher.prompt: How does a topic sentence help a reader?

activities.title: Choose the Most Precise Sentence
activities.skill: Choose the sentence with the strongest details
activities.directions: A student is writing about a science walk. Read the four sentences. Choose the one with the most precise, detailed words.
activities.prompt: Which sentence is the most precise and detailed?

options.text: We saw a nice thing outside.
An orange monarch butterfly landed gently on the purple flowers by the fence.
There was a bug and it was on some stuff.

vocabulary: a small fact that makes writing clearer
detalle: un dato pequeño que hace la escritura más clara
mariposa monarca: una mariposa anaranjada y negra
frames: The most precise sentence tells ___, ___, and ___.
activities.correct: Yes! It names exactly what, how, and where — that is precise writing.
activities.hint: Look for the sentence that answers what, how, and where with exact words.
activities.support: Vague words: thing, stuff, nice, went. Precise words name exactly what you mean.
activities.extension: Rewrite one of the weaker sentences to make it precise.

teacher.use: Revision skill: word choice and detail.
teacher.function: Inform — precise nouns, verbs, and phrases.
teacher.lower: Underline the nouns and verbs in each choice.
teacher.onLevel: Students choose and explain what makes it stronger.
teacher.challenge: Students revise the other three sentences.
teacher.noTech: Print and circle; revise one sentence.
teacher.prompt: What words did you notice in the strongest sentence?

sheet.heading: Check

vocabulary: a word that connects ideas, like also or as a result
transición: una palabra que conecta ideas, como también o como resultado

teacher.use: Printable planner for informational writing.

sheet.heading: My opinion
items: Every student should / should not learn a second language (circle one).

argumentar: dar razones de lo que crees
